output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely a cooling failure, not a contractor or kiosk problem. One chiller serving floors 6-8 failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1, and scores recovered once cooling returned. Floors 1-5 stayed flat. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and cleanliness complaints did not change after Orrin took over, so there is no evidence against Orrin. Check-in scores, kiosk complaints and queue times are also flat, so the kiosks are not the cause. The survey questionnaire and invitation process were unchanged. The 6% rate rise may have nudged value scores down a little on floors 1-5, but that can't be separated from the usual August dip. I am fairly confident (about 85-90%). Next steps: don't serve notice on Orrin, don't pull the kiosks, and don't drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. Reinstate the deferred chiller maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A follow-up offer to affected guests is reasonable, though they already received an apology and a half-night credit. Keep watching value scores before touching the rates.
